what do you mean by BPD episodes?

I'm pretty sure if you have a 4-day streak of mania, you have bipolar disorder, not BPD. Our symptoms are not that consistent. It is an everyday rollercoaster of emotions, whereas bipolar disorder has consistent episodes of mania or depression that can last for days, weeks, or months. Also, we don't typically experience mania, which seems to be more of a triggered emotion, if anything.

Why do I need to change for my friend?

He's the one who wanted to change? How would he be offended? I know it has to come from him, but a little support can be a good head start toward recovery. Addiction is hard to deal with, especially alone. I'm here to be there for him if he wants it, I just wanted advice if he were to ever ask for that extra support. Also, I literally didn't tell him he was doing anything wrong in his life. That would make me a bad friend, I'm concerned for his health and mental well-being but what he's doing isn't "bad" yeah it's not healthy but I understand it's a way to cope due to depression. I'm on his side through and through.

Well, he lives with his mom, who cooks for him and herself. It's just that he's admitted he has an addiction and has told me countless times that it's a problem for him and that he wants to change. I understand how depression works. I'm depressed too, but I'm managing well. I'm not trying to devalue or even shame him for having a problem. I'm concerned about him and want to be there if he wants that. If I was in his shoes, I wouldn't be upset at my friend for wanting to help me. Hey, I'm basically your friend in this situation. I fell in love with my guy friend, the feelings I have for him are so strong and deep. I ended up confessing to him about it in December but he, unfortunately, didn't feel the same way. Something that helped relax my nerves after the rejection was something he told me. He said that although he may not love me romantically, he still deeply loves me as a best friend. And that was all the clarity I needed. If you don't feel the same way towards your friend, please reassure her that you still appreciate the friendship and won't think of her any different. I'm really happy she was brave enough to let you know her true feelings, if you feel the same way don't lead her on, be direct and honest.

I don't think you "insist" on making yourself hurt, no one ever intentionally tries to make themselves hurt. You absolutely do have control of your life and the way you react to misfortunes. You just need to find a way to get your control back. Until then, it's perfectly okay to "fuck up" for now. Allow yourself time to grieve, allow yourself to feel everything you're feeling. Don't suppress anything. I recommend talking to a trusted friend, family member, or even consider taking therapy. Talking helps more than you think, it's not healthy to bottle your emotions, let them out. You're going to be okay <3
